阻塞整个事件循环\n    return response\n```\n\n3. 模型调用执行期间，**所有其他 FastAPI 端点均无响应**（健康检查、WebSocket 连接等全部挂起）。\n\n**期望行为**\n\n多模态路径应使用 `await dashscope.AioMultiModalConversation.call()`（DashScope SDK 已提供），避免阻塞 asyncio 事件循环，与非多模态路径行为保持一致。\n\n**根因分析**\n\n[src/agentscope/model/_dashscope_model.py](cci:7://file:///D:/work/worknote/project/TeachingAnalyzer/agentscope/src/agentscope/model/_dashscope_model.py:0:0-0:0) 第 273 行：\n\n```python\n# 当前代码（阻塞）：\nresponse = dashscope.MultiModalConversation.call(\n    api_key=self.api_key,\n    **kwargs,\n)\n\n# 期望代码（非阻塞）：\nresponse = await dashscope.AioMultiModalConversation.call(\n    api_key=self.api_key,\n    **kwargs,\n)\n```\n\n两个 API 签名完全一致，唯一区别：\n- `MultiModalConversation.call()` → 同步函数，返回 `Response | Generator`\n- `AioMultiModalConversation.call()` → 异步协程，返回 `Response | AsyncGenerator`\n\n下游 [_parse_dashscope_stream_response](cci:1://file:///d:/work/worknote/project/Professional%20evaluation/agentscope/src/agentscope/model/_dashscope_model.py:299:4-477:13) 的类型标注已包含 `Union[AsyncGenerator, Generator]`，因此修改应该是向后兼容的。\n\n**错误信息**\n\n无显式错误信息。表现为 asyncio 事件循环被阻塞，导致所有并发异步任务（HTTP 处理器、WebSocket 连接、后台任务）在同步 API 调用完成前全部停滞。\n\n**环境信息：**\n\n- AgentScope 版本：1.0.16\n- Python 版本：3.11.14\n- 操作系统：Windows 11\n- DashScope SDK 版本：最新\n\n**补充说明**\n\n- 同步 MultiModalConversation.call() 调用在 PR #1215 之前就已存在（用于 qvq/-vl 模型名自动检测场景）。PR #1215 添加了 multimodality 参数使其可显式控制，但未将底层调用更新为异步版本 AioMultiModalConversation.call()，使得该同步阻塞问题扩展到了更多模型场景。\n- 修复仅需一行代码：将 `dashscope.MultiModalConversation.call(` 替换为 `await dashscope.AioMultiModalConversation.call(`。\n- 目前我们通过 `asyncio.run_in_executor()` 将同步调用放入线程池作为临时方案，但这增加了不必要的复杂性。\n",

`post_model_hook` in `create_react_agent` the injection of state/store into the tool calls is not performed.\nAny reliance on state in a tool for such an agent will fail the pydantic input args validations.\n\nCause of the problem is here:\nIn langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py\nThe code of [`post_model_hook_router`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/2553ae0b877c58beb8947db70336c008d7c7ea23/libs/prebuilt/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py#L709) decides if a tool execution is required, and will use `Send` to route to the tool node like so:\n```python\nreturn [Send(\"tools\", [tool_call]) for tool_call in pending_tool_calls]\n```\n\nComparing that with the [`should_continue`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/2553ae0b877c58beb8947db70336c008d7c7ea23/libs/prebuilt/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py#L632) implementation, When there is no \"post_model_hook\" setup it will `Send` to the tools node like so:\n```python\ntool_calls = [\n    tool_node.inject_tool_args(call, state, store)  # type: ignore[arg-type]\n    for call in last_message.tool_calls\n]\nreturn [Send(\"tools\", [tool_call]) for tool_call in tool_calls]\n```\n\nSo, when the hook is setup you get the flow:\nagent -> should_continue -> post_model_hook -> post_model_hook_router -> tools\nAnd without you get:\nagent -> should_continue -> tools\n\nThe first, will neglect to inject a state/store and the latter will.\nI believe this is a bug.\nIdeally, there will be a single \"send to tools\" implementation which both routers should use.\n\n### System Info\n\nSystem Information\n------------------\n> OS:  Darwin\n> OS Version:  Darwin Kernel Version   "problem_statement": "[BUG] CrewAI Decorators Don't Support Async Methods - Causes \"'coroutine' object has no attribute 'name'\" Error\n### Description\n\n## Summary\nCrewAI's `@agent`, `@task`, and `@crew` decorators do not properly support async methods. When decorating async methods that return coroutines, the decorators fail to unwrap the coroutine, resulting in the error: `'coroutine' object has no attribute 'name'`.\n\n## Environment\n- **OS**: Ubuntu 22.04 (Docker)\n- **Python Version**: 3.13.0\n- **CrewAI Version**: 0.62.2\n- **Framework**: FastAPI + Telegram Bot (aiogram) + AsyncSQLAlchemy 2.0\n\n## Description\nWe're building an async-first architecture where CrewAI crews are executed within FastAPI/Telegram handlers. Tool initialization requires async database operations via AsyncSession, so we need async tool creation.\n\n**Problem Flow:**\n1. We decorated agent/task methods with `async def` to support `await self._create_tools()`\n2. The `@agent`, `@task`, `@crew` decorators don't await the async methods\n3. This returns a coroutine object instead of Agent/Task/Crew instances\n4. When CrewAI tries to access `.name` attribute on the coroutine, it fails\n\n### Error Stack\n```\nERROR | src.agents.tools.base:run_crew_isolated:141 - Crew execution failed | \ncrew_class=FounderCrew run_mode=answer error='coroutine' object has no attribute 'name'\n\nTraceback:\n  File \"src/agents/tools/base.py\", line 135, in run_crew_isolated\n    result = crew_instance.crew(run_mode).kickoff_async(inputs)\nAttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'name'\n```\n\n## Workaround Attempted\nWe tried wrapping async `_arun()` calls in a sync `_run()` fallback:\n\n```python\ndef _run(self, *args, **kwargs):\n    return run_async(self._arun(*args, **kwargs))  # ❌ Creates new event loop → loop conflicts\n```\n\nThis reintroduces \"Task got Future attached to a different loop\" errors because it spawns a new event loop inside the existing one.\n\n## Root Cause Analysis\nThe `@agent`, `@task`, and `@crew` decorators use class method introspection but don't check if the method is a coroutine function. They should either:\n\n1. **Auto-await async methods** (recommended for modern Python):\n```python\ndef decorator(method):\n    def wrapper(self):\n        result = method(self)\n        if asyncio.iscoroutine(result):\n            return asyncio.run(result)  # Or: await result in async context\n        return result\n    return wrapper\n```\n\n2. **Explicitly reject async methods** with helpful error:\n```python\ndef decorator(method):\n    if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(method):\n        raise TypeError(\n            f\"Method '{method.__name__}' is async but @agent/@task/@crew \"\n            \"decorators only support sync methods. \"\n            \"Create tools synchronously or use a different pattern.\"\n        )\n    return original_decorator(method)\n```\n\n## Questions for CrewAI Team\n1. Are `@agent`, `@task`, `@crew` decorators intentionally limited to sync-only?\n2. Is there a supported pattern for async tool creation in async-first applications?\n3. Would a PR adding async support to decorators be welcome?\n4. Should we await async methods at decoration time or at call time?\n\n## Production Context\nThis is a production issue affecting:\n- **Telegram Bot** (aiogram) with async handlers\n- **FastAPI** application with async endpoints  \n- **AsyncSQLAlchemy** database operations\n- **PostgreSQL** via asyncpg driver\n\nWe need async-safe tool execution to avoid event loop conflicts and zombie database connections.\n\n## Proposed Solution\nAdd async method detection and auto-await to the decorators:\n\n```python\n# In crewai/decorators.py or similar\nimport asyncio\nfrom functools import wraps\n\ndef agent(method):\n    @wraps(method)\n    def wrapper(self, *args, **kwargs):\n        result = method(self, *args, **kwargs)\n        if asyncio.iscoroutine(result):\n            # Option 1: Run in current event loop (if in async context)\n            try:\n                loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()\n                # Schedule as task if already in event loop\n                return asyncio.ensure_future(result)\n            except RuntimeError:\n                # No running loop - run new one\n                return asyncio.run(result)\n        return result\n    return wrapper\n```\n\nThis allows developers to write naturally async code while maintaining backward compatibility.\n\n### Steps to Reproduce\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n\n### Code Example\n```python\nfrom crewai import Agent, Task, Crew\nfrom crewai.task import Task\nfrom crewai.agent import Agent\n\nclass FounderCrew:\n    @agent\n    async def your-agent(self) -> Agent:\n        \"\"\"This is the problem -   "hints_text": "<!-- Greeting -->\nHi @cpu-16! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the langflow team.\n\n<!-- Answer -->\nThis happens because LangFlow always includes `\"mirostat\": 0` in the parameters sent to the Ollama API when Mirostat is set to \"Disabled\". Ollama expects the `mirostat` parameter to be omitted entirely when not in use—sending it with a value of 0 causes an invalid option error. The same applies to related parameters like `mirostat_eta` and `mirostat_tau` when Mirostat is disabled.\n\nTo fix this, the parameter-building logic in LangFlow's Ollama integration (specifically the `build_model` method) should only include `mirostat`, `mirostat_eta`, and `mirostat_tau` when Mirostat is enabled (i.e., not \"Disabled\" or 0). Right now, only parameters set to `None` are omitted, but parameters set to 0 are still sent, which is not compatible with Ollama's API requirements. This is a localized, low-risk change in the backend code and will resolve the integration error you’re seeing [reference](https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/blob/15f44519af6a414299d74516aa69f4c895235b69/src/backend/base/langflow/components/languagemodels/ollama.py).\n\nThere’s currently no documentation or open issues in the repo that address this parameter handling for Ollama models. │     • Single or multiple services can be created via               │

│       dependencies recursively.                                    │
│     • Services are instantiated via their corresponding factory's  │
│       create() method with dependency injection of already created │
│       services.                                                    │
│     • Services have lifecycle methods like set_ready() after       │

│        • Registers the Settings service factory                    │

│     • initialize_session_service():                                │
│        • Calls initialize_settings_service() first.                │
│        • Registers the Cache service factory                       │
│          (CacheServiceFactory).                                    │
│        • Registers the Session service factory                     │
│          (SessionServiceFactory).                                  │

│     • Caching is handled via a dedicated cache service factory     │
│       (CacheServiceFactory) registered during                      │
│       initialize_session_service().                                │
│     • The Cache service becomes a dependency that can be injected  │

│     • Factory modules are imported dynamically from                │
│       "langflow.services.<service_name>.factory".                  │
│     • Subclasses of ServiceFactory are instantiated automatically  │
│       and registered.                                              │

│  • User-related API endpoints and their usage:                     │
│     1 POST / (Add new user)                                        │
│        • Input: UserCreate schema                                  │
│        • Output: UserRead schema                                   │
│        • Functionality: Creates a new user, hashes password, sets  │
│          user active state based on settings, commits to DB,       │
│          creates default folder                                    │
│        • Errors: 400 if username is taken, 500 if default folder   │
│          creation fails                                            │
│     2 GET /whoami (Get current user)                               │
│        • Output: UserRead                                          │
│        • Depends on current authenticated active user              │
│        • Returns currently authenticated user's data               │
│     3 GET / (List users)                                           │
│        • Query Params: skip (int, default 0), limit (int, default  │
│          10)                                                       │
│        • Output: UsersResponse containing total count and list of  │
│          UserRead users                                            │
│        • Access restricted to superusers only                      │
│     4 PATCH /{user_id} (Update user partially)                     │
│        • URL Param: user_id (UUID)                                 │
│        • Input: UserUpdate                                         │
│        • Output: UserRead                                          │
│        • Permissions:                                              │
│           • Only superusers can change is_superuser flag or update │
│             other users                                            │
│           • Regular users can update themselves except changing    │
│             password here                                          │
│        • Password change requires superuser permission (hashing    │
│          done automatically if changed)                            │
│        • Returns updated user or 404 if user not found             │
│     5 PATCH /{user_id}/reset-password (Reset password)             │
│        • URL Param: user_id (UUID)                                 │
│        • Input: UserUpdate (with password)                         │
│        • Output: UserRead                                          │
│        • Only allows resetting own password                        │
│        • Cannot reuse current password                             │
│     6 DELETE /{user_id} (Delete user)                              │
│        • URL Param: user_id (UUID)                                 │
│        • Output: dict with detail message                          │
│        • Permissions:                                              │
│           • Only superusers can delete users                       │
│           • Cannot delete own user account                         │
│        • Returns error if user not found or permission denied      │
│  • Authentication & Authorization:                                 │
│     • Uses FastAPI Depends for getting current active user or      │
│       superuser                                                    │
│     • Password hashing and verification via get_password_hash and  │
│       verify_password                                              │
│  • DB Interaction:                                                 │
│     • Uses SQLModel Session and queries for User model             │
│     • Transaction handling with commit and rollback on errors      │
│                                                                    │
│ Summary: The User API exposes typical user management operations   │
│ via REST endpoints, with distinct permission controls ensuring     │
│ only superusers can list all users, update others, or delete       │
│ accounts, while regular users can read their own info and reset    │
│ their own password. Password handling is secure, and user creation │
